title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
authors: Jegadeesh, N., & Titman, S.
source: Journal of Finance (original paywalled); accessible via University of Houston mirror
note: The foundational cross-sectional momentum paper. Original 1993 Journal of Finance publication is paywalled; a stable university mirror provides the full text.

title: Time Series Momentum
authors: Moskowitz, T. J., Ooi, Y. H., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: The single most-cited foundational paper on trend-following/time-series momentum. Directly grounds SMA(10/30) crossover.

title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
authors: De Bondt, W. F. M., & Thaler, R.
source: Journal of Finance -- PAYWALLED, no verified legitimate free copy found
note: The foundational overreaction/reversal paper. Cited by finding and title only -- the only accessible copy found was an unverified mirror site, not used per this project's source-integrity standard.

title: Mean Reversion in Stock Prices: Evidence and Implications
authors: Poterba, J. M., & Summers, L. H.
note: Official NBER PDF, freely available. Second independent source on mean-reversion, alongside De Bondt & Thaler's finding.

title: A Closer Look at the Short-Term Return Reversal
authors: Da, Z., Liu, Q., & Schaumburg, E.
source: Management Science, Vol. 60, Issue 3, pp. 658-674 (DOI: 10.1287/mnsc.2013.1766); open PDF (nd.edu / informs.org)
note: Confirms and extends Jegadeesh's original short-term reversal finding. Third source on mean-reversion for robustness.

title: Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage: Understanding the Low-Volatility Anomaly
authors: Baker, M., Bradley, B., & Wurgler, J.
note: Foundational low-volatility anomaly paper. Grounds the regime classifier's high/low-vol distinction.

title: Betting Against Beta
authors: Frazzini, A., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: Official NBER PDF. Second, independent source on the low-volatility/low-beta effect.

title: The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
authors: Fama, E. F., & French, K. R.
note: Foundational value/size-factor paper, hosted on a business-school faculty course page (same category of legitimate hosting as NYU Stern/Duke pages already used).

title: Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk
authors: Lakonishok, J., Shleifer, A., & Vishny, R. W.
note: Official NBER PDF. Second value-family source.

title: Quality Minus Junk
authors: Asness, C., Frazzini, A., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: Foundational quality-factor paper.

title: The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium
authors: Novy-Marx, R.
source: author's own University of Rochester page
note: Second quality-family source, hosted directly by the author.

title: Capital Market Seasonality: The Case of Stock Returns
authors: Rozeff, M. S., & Kinney, W. R.
source: Journal of Financial Economics (Elsevier) -- PAYWALLED, no free copy found
note: The original January-effect paper. Cited by finding and title only -- genuinely paywalled at Elsevier with no legitimate free copy found.

title: The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle
authors: Bouman, S., & Jacobsen, B.
source: American Economic Review; a PDF link exists via Semantic Scholar, provenance unverified
note: A PDF link was found but could not be independently verified as an authorized copy before ingestion. Confirm manually before placing in data/corpus/raw/.

title: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
authors: Harvey, C. R., Liu, Y., & Zhu, H.
note: Foundational paper on multiple-hypothesis-testing corrections in finance. Academic justification for research_stats.multiple_comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg) already built in Stage 4.

title: Publication Bias in Asset Pricing Research
authors: Chen, A. Y., & Zimmermann, T.
note: The only arXiv-native paper in this batch -- auto-fetchable via the arXiv API. Offers a more moderate counterpoint to Harvey/Liu/Zhu's stricter significance hurdle, giving balanced methodological grounding rather than a one-sided view.

title: A comparative study of the MACD-base trading strategies: evidence from the US stock market
authors: Pat Tong Chio
note: Comparative empirical study of MACD-based trading strategies on US equities. MACD is trend-following/momentum; no existing KNOWN_STRATEGIES rule uses it directly (confirmed by checking backtester/schema.py directly -- only SMA_CROSSOVER, RSI_14_30_70, RSI_2_10_90, and MORNING_STAR exist), so grounds is empty rather than forced onto an unrelated rule.

title: VolTS: A Volatility-based Trading System to forecast Stock Markets Trend using Statistics and Machine Learning
authors: Letteri, I.
note: Volatility-based trading system combining statistics and machine learning. Grounds the regime classifier's volatility-regime distinction, alongside baker_bradley_wurgler_lowvol and frazzini_pedersen_2014.

title: Algorithmic Trading Strategy Development and Optimisation
authors: Owen Nyo Wei Yuan, Victor Tan Jia Xuan, Ong Jun Yao Fabian, & Ryan Tan Jun Wei
note: General algorithmic trading strategy paper combining moving averages, momentum, volatility indicators, and FinBERT sentiment analysis on S&P 500 data (confirmed from the real abstract). Originally proposed as an 'ATR-bucketing' paper -- confirmed real and genuinely on-topic, but the actual abstract does not mention ATR or bucketing specifically. That characterization could not be verified and should NOT be cited as grounding that particular technique; tagged momentum/volatility broadly instead.

title: New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems
authors: Wilder, J. W.
source: Practitioner book (Trend Research); pre-dates open-access norms, no legitimate free copy found
note: The original source introducing RSI -- cited directly as literature_source for RSI_14_30_70 in backtester/schema.py's KNOWN_STRATEGIES (confirmed by reading the code directly, line 215). Its prior absence from this corpus was a real inconsistency between the code and the catalog. Cited by title only; a 1978 practitioner book has no legitimate open-access copy. grounds is rsi_14_30_70 only, not rsi_2_10_90 -- narrower and more accurate than the existing three mean-reversion entries, which ground both, since the code attributes each RSI rule to a different, specific source.

title: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work: A Quantified Guide to Trading Stocks and ETF's
authors: Connors, L. A., & Alvarez, C.
source: Practitioner book (Connors Research); no legitimate free copy found
note: Cited directly as literature_source for RSI_2_10_90, the short-horizon RSI(2) mean-reversion rule, in backtester/schema.py's KNOWN_STRATEGIES (confirmed by reading the code directly, line 227). Its prior absence from this corpus was a real inconsistency between the code and the catalog. Cited by title only; no legitimate open-access copy of this book exists. grounds is rsi_2_10_90 only, not rsi_14_30_70 -- see wilder_1978's own note for why this is deliberately narrower than the existing mean-reversion entries.
